newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slumber, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slumber, volume thin.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities edged lower amid very thin volume on Monday, mortgage experts said.
Seasoned, premium-coupon collateral traded earlier in the morning, but market activity virtually came to a grinding halt by late afternoon, they said.
"(Volume) is as thin as I've ever seen it," said one trader at a New York-based investment firm.
Another trader at a large retail shop on the East Coast said most of his trades were odd lots.
"There were tons of odd lot lists, high numbers of pools," he said. "I haven't seen anything with substance really coming through," he added.
At 1545 EST/2045 GMT, pass-throughs were flat to 2/32 lower, and spreads over Treasuries held largely unchanged.
In specific coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 1/32 at 99-29/32, yielding 98 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was off 1/32 at 99-29/32, and the Freddie Mac current coupon was 2/32 lower, at 100-02/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 1/32 at 97-27/32 bid.
